# Lab 15.6: Graph Measures & Hybrid Analysis

## What We Are Going to Do
Add a measure to the graph (Preview) and combine graph results with vector search and AI functions in one analysis.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Add a measure.** A measure defines a business metric once, so it is always aggregated the same way:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE OR REPLACE PROPERTY GRAPH lab15.FinGraphM
  NODE TABLES (lab15.Person LABEL Person, lab15.Account LABEL Account)
  EDGE TABLES (
    lab15.PersonOwnAccount SOURCE KEY (id) REFERENCES Person (id)
      DESTINATION KEY (account_id) REFERENCES Account (id) LABEL Owns,
    lab15.AccountTransferAccount SOURCE KEY (id) REFERENCES Account (id)
      DESTINATION KEY (to_id) REFERENCES Account (id)
      LABEL Transfers PROPERTIES (amount, create_time, MEASURE(SUM(amount)) AS total_amount)
  );</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Measures are Preview and not available in Standard edition. If the syntax is rejected, check **GQL schema statements** in the docs for the current form.

2. **[SQL] Graph + AI.** Ask Gemini to explain each risky pattern:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT owner, account, amount,
  AI.GENERATE(CONCAT('In one sentence, explain why a transfer of ', CAST(amount AS STRING),
                     ' from ', owner, ' into a blocked account could be risky.')).result AS explanation
FROM GRAPH_TABLE(lab15.FinGraph
  MATCH (p:Person)-[:Owns]-&gt;(a:Account)-[t:Transfers]-&gt;(:Account {is_blocked: TRUE})
  COLUMNS (p.name AS owner, a.id AS account, t.amount AS amount));</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[SQL] Graph + vector search.** Find people whose city name is semantically close to "coastal city in western India", then expand their transfers in the graph:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">WITH close_people AS (
  SELECT name FROM lab15.Person
  ORDER BY AI.SIMILARITY('coastal city in western India', city, model =&gt; 'embeddinggemma-300m') DESC
  LIMIT 2
)
SELECT g.* FROM GRAPH_TABLE(lab15.FinGraph
  MATCH (p:Person)-[:Owns]-&gt;(a:Account)-[t:Transfers]-&gt;(b:Account)
  COLUMNS (p.name AS name, a.id AS from_acc, b.id AS to_acc, t.amount AS amount)) g
JOIN close_people USING (name);</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[Console] Chat with the graph.** Conversational analytics can use graphs as a source (Module 16). Add `lab15.FinGraph` to a data agent and ask *"Which accounts are part of a transfer loop?"*
